Plain text only: no markup. Add terms rather than rewording existing ones so reports stay consistent run to run.

terms.10-K: A public company's audited annual report filed with the SEC.
terms.10-Q: A public company's quarterly financial report filed with the SEC.
terms.accredited investor: Someone meeting SEC income or net-worth thresholds, and therefore allowed to buy private offerings.
terms.ACS: American Community Survey - the US Census Bureau's rolling survey. Its 5-year tables are the standard data source for testing whether an area's unemployment is high enough to qualify for the $800,000 price.
terms.adjudication: The formal decision USCIS makes on a petition or application.
terms.APN: Assessor's Parcel Number - the county's unique ID for a piece of land. It ties a project to an exact mapped boundary, and therefore to an exact census tract.
terms.at-risk: Your money must be genuinely exposed to loss, with no guaranteed return, for at least two years. Any promise to repay you can invalidate the petition.
terms.bridge: Short-term financing used to start a project before permanent money arrives. USCIS permits EB-5 capital to replace it and still count the jobs, if the paperwork supports it.
terms.cap rate: The rate used to convert a property's annual profit into a value. A higher cap rate means a lower value.
terms.capital stack: The layers of money funding a project, from the most protected (senior debt) to the least (equity). Your position in it decides who loses money first.
terms.census tract: A small Census Bureau statistical area, typically 1,200-8,000 people. EB-5 high-unemployment areas are defined by census tracts, so which tract a project sits in decides whether it qualifies.
terms.chargeability: The country a visa applicant counts against - normally the country of birth, not citizenship. It determines whether you face a queue.
terms.civilian labor force: Everyone working or actively looking for work, excluding the military and people not seeking a job. It is the denominator of the unemployment rate.
terms.completion guaranty: A promise to finish the building. Note it is NOT a promise to repay your money.
terms.conditional permanent resident: The two-year provisional green card you receive when your I-526E is approved. It becomes permanent only after the I-829 is granted.
terms.confidence: This report's 0-3 rating of how well a finding is evidenced: 3 is a government record, 0 is the sponsor's word alone.
terms.curable: A defect the sponsor could still fix - typically by producing the real document. If they will not, that refusal is itself a finding.
terms.debt yield: Annual operating profit divided by the loan amount. Lenders typically want about 11% on hotels before they will refinance.
terms.directly adjacent: Sharing a boundary with the project's own census tract. The law lets a project average its tract together with directly adjacent ones - but not chain outward tract by tract until the number works.
terms.disposition: This report's call on what to actually do about a finding: ACCEPT (note it, do not let it delay you), CAUTION (one check before you wire), MITIGATE (get something specific in writing first), or AVOID (walk away).
terms.EB-5: The US immigrant investor visa. Invest $800,000 (or $1,050,000 outside a targeted employment area) in a business that creates at least 10 full-time American jobs, and you and your immediate family can obtain green cards.
terms.EDGAR: The SEC's free public database of company and fund filings.
terms.entitlement: The land-use approvals that make it legal to build what is planned. Without them a project cannot lawfully start.
terms.escrow: A neutral third party holds your money and releases it only when agreed conditions are met, such as your petition being filed or approved.
terms.first lien: A first legal claim over the property. If the borrower defaults, first-lien lenders are paid before anyone else from a sale.
terms.Form ADV: The disclosure document every SEC-registered investment adviser must file, covering fees, conflicts and disciplinary history.
terms.Form D: A brief notice filed with the SEC when securities are sold privately. It shows the offering size and how much has been sold.
terms.full funding: Whether the project actually raised all the money its plan requires. A gap between sources and uses is a live ground for USCIS to question the plan.
terms.fund administrator: An independent firm that controls and reports on the movement of investor money. The 2022 reform law requires this or an annual audit.
terms.going concern: A formal warning in audited accounts that there is substantial doubt the company can survive the next twelve months.
terms.hard gate: In this report, a finding serious enough to force a NO-GO on its own, regardless of every other score.
terms.high-unemployment: The other route to the $800,000 price: the site's census tract, averaged with directly adjacent tracts, must show unemployment at least 150% of the national rate. Harder to verify than rural because the developer picks which adjacent tracts to average in and rarely says which - so it is checked by re-deriving it from the parcel. Valid designations are fine; the trade-off against rural is a slower queue, not a weaker petition.
terms.I-526E: Your individual petition as an investor in a regional-center project. Approval gets you a conditional green card.
terms.I-797: The paper notice USCIS issues to confirm a receipt, an approval or a denial. It is the document to ask for as proof.
terms.I-829: The petition filed about two years later to remove the conditions on your green card. This is where job creation is finally tested.
terms.I-924A: The annual report older regional centers had to file before the 2022 reform law replaced it with the I-956G.
terms.I-956F: The project's own application to USCIS, filed by the regional center. It must be FILED before any investor can submit an I-526E, and approved before any I-526E can be approved.
terms.I-956G: The annual statement every regional center must file with USCIS. Missing it is grounds for termination.
terms.I-956K: The registration form third-party promoters and overseas migration agents must file with USCIS under the 2022 reform law.
terms.IMPLAN: One of the economic models USCIS accepts for estimating how many jobs a project's spending creates.
terms.indirect: Jobs created in the wider economy by a project's spending, calculated by an economic model rather than counted on a payroll.
terms.induced: Jobs created when workers spend their wages locally. Like indirect jobs, these are modelled rather than counted.
terms.JCE: Job Creating Entity: the business that actually spends the money and creates the jobs your green card depends on, usually the developer's project company.
terms.job cushion: How far projected jobs exceed the 10-per-investor minimum. A thin cushion means small cost savings or delays can cause a shortfall.
terms.LPA: Limited Partnership Agreement: the contract governing the fund, including redeployment and voting rights.
terms.material change: A change to a project big enough that USCIS may no longer treat the approved project as the one you invested in. Increases in scope are riskier than decreases.
terms.Metropolitan: In this context, an OMB-defined metro region built around an urban core of 50,000 or more people. Being inside one disqualifies a site from the rural category.
terms.Metropolitan Statistical Area: An OMB-defined metro region built around an urban core of 50,000 or more. Being inside one disqualifies a site from the rural category.
terms.mezzanine: A layer of debt sitting between senior debt and equity. Riskier than senior debt, safer than equity.
terms.Micropolitan: A Census area built around a town of 10,000-50,000 people. Crucially a micropolitan area is NOT a Metropolitan Statistical Area, so a site inside one can still qualify as rural.
terms.micropolitan: A Census area built around a town of 10,000-50,000 people. It is NOT a Metropolitan Statistical Area, so a site inside one can still qualify as rural.
terms.Nasdaq: The US stock exchange. A company listed on it must file audited financial statements publicly.
terms.NCE: New Commercial Enterprise: the fund or partnership you actually invest into. It then lends or invests the pooled money into the project.
terms.NOIT: Notice of Intent to Terminate, the warning USCIS sends a regional center before revoking its designation.
terms.parcel: The specific piece of land, identified by an assessor's parcel number (APN), that the project company actually owns. Pinning the tract from the parcel is reliable; pinning it from a street address or an intersection is not.
terms.plat: The recorded legal map dividing land into lots. Required before individual lots can be sold.
terms.PPM: Private Placement Memorandum: the main legal offering document, containing the terms and risk factors.
terms.priority processing: Faster USCIS handling. The 2022 law directs it for RURAL projects only; high-unemployment projects get no such priority.
terms.probability band: How likely the harm is to actually happen, from P0 (remote, under 5%) to P4 (near-certain, over 80%). P4 means it is already true on the record, not a forecast.
terms.proration: Counting only part of the jobs. Where construction runs under two years, the direct construction jobs count only in proportion to the months of building.
terms.PUD: Planned Unit Development: a custom zoning approval that lets a developer build at a density the standard zoning does not allow.
terms.redeployment: If the project repays the loan before your conditions are removed, the fund must reinvest your money in something else to keep it at risk. Where and for how long is set by the partnership agreement.
terms.REDYN: Another economic model used for EB-5 job estimates. Less commonly adjudicated by USCIS than IMPLAN or RIMS-II.
terms.Reg D: The SEC rules allowing private offerings to be sold without full public registration.
terms.regional center: A USCIS-designated organisation licensed to sponsor EB-5 projects in a defined geographic area. Using one lets investors count indirect and induced jobs, not just employees on a payroll.
terms.Regional Center: A USCIS-designated organisation licensed to sponsor EB-5 projects in a defined geographic area. Using one lets investors count indirect and induced jobs, not just employees on a payroll.
terms.repayment guaranty: A promise to repay the loan. Much stronger for an investor than a completion guaranty, and much rarer.
terms.reserved category: The 32% of EB-5 visas set aside each year for rural (20%), high-unemployment (10%) and infrastructure (2%) projects.
terms.residual risk: What is left after you apply the mitigations you can actually obtain. It is often a better guide to which deal to pick than the raw score.
terms.retrogression: When more people apply in a visa category than there are visas, a queue forms and the cut-off date moves backwards. The high-unemployment set-aside is half the size of the rural one, so it fills up first.
terms.RevPAR: Revenue per available room: the standard hotel measure combining occupancy and room rate.
terms.RIA: The EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022, which rewrote the programme: it created the reserved visa categories, the two-year at-risk rule, mandatory fund administration or audit, and the I-956F project approval.
terms.rural: For EB-5, a site outside every Metropolitan Statistical Area AND outside any city or town of 20,000 or more people. Both tests must be met. It is pure geography, so anyone can verify it independently.
terms.senior: The most protected layer of a project's funding, repaid before everyone else and usually secured against the property.
terms.set-aside: The share of EB-5 visas reserved each year for particular project types: 20% for rural, 10% for high-unemployment, 2% for infrastructure. Reserved categories have far shorter queues than the general one, but the smaller high-unemployment pool fills up sooner.
terms.severity class: How bad it is if it does happen, from S1 (friction only) to S4 (green-card fatal or total loss of the $800,000).
terms.source-of-funds: The evidence trail proving your investment money was lawfully earned and lawfully transferred.
terms.stabilisation: The point at which a newly opened property reaches its expected normal level of occupancy and profit.
terms.stabilization: The point at which a newly opened property reaches its expected normal level of occupancy and profit.
terms.STR: The hotel industry's standard benchmarking service, which publishes occupancy and rate data for competing hotels.
terms.structural: A defect with no fix available to you before your deadline - a wall. Contrast a curable one, which is the opening of a negotiation with the sponsor.
terms.sustainment: The requirement that your capital stays invested and at risk for at least two years from when it is made available to the project.
terms.takeout: The event that repays the loan at maturity, normally a refinance or a sale. A loan with no committed takeout depends on hope.
terms.TEA: Targeted Employment Area. A site that is either rural, or has unemployment at least 150% of the national average. Investing in one lowers the minimum from $1,050,000 to $800,000 and unlocks a reserved visa queue.
terms.USCIS: US Citizenship and Immigration Services, the government agency that decides EB-5 petitions.
terms.Visa Bulletin: The State Department's monthly notice of which visa categories are current and which have a backlog. It is where you check whether your country of birth faces a wait.
terms.weighted average: An average that gives bigger areas more influence. For a high-unemployment area the tracts are weighted by the size of their labour force, so one small high-unemployment tract cannot carry several large low-unemployment neighbours.
